Tests of the provider effects of a linear fixed-effect fit

Source: R/test_linear_fe.R
test.linear_fe.Rd

Wald tests of \(H_0: \gamma_i = \gamma_0\) for every provider (or a subset) with the model-based or the patient-clustered standard error.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'linear_fe'
test(
  fit,
  variance = c("naive", "robust"),
  null = "median",
  providers = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  wald_variance = c("case_mix", "full"),
  null_model = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted by fit_linear_fe().

variance

"naive" (default; model-based, see gamma_variance()) or "robust" (patient-clustered sandwich with \(\hat\beta\) held fixed; needs a patient column in pp_data()).

null

the null value \(\gamma_0\): "median" (default) or "mean" (weighted by rows) of the fitted effects, or a number.

providers

optional subset of provider identifiers to report.

level

confidence level; the significance level is 1 - level.

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

wald_variance

for variance = "naive": "case_mix" (default) or "full", see gamma_variance().

null_model

optional null model (a pp_null object or a function of the result returning one), applied through calibrate().

...

unused.

Value

A data frame of class pp_test with the columns described in test.logistic_fe().

Details

The naive statistic \((\hat\gamma_i - \gamma_0) / se_i\) is referred to the t distribution with \(n - m - p\) degrees of freedom, the robust statistic to the standard normal. The robust standard error is \(\sqrt{\sum_{k \in i} (\sum_{j \in k} e_{ij})^2} / n_i\) over the provider's patients \(k\), with \(e_{ij}\) the residuals: the sandwich variance of \(\bar Y_i - \bar Z_i^\top\hat\beta\).

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, type = "continuous", seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_linear_fe(pd)
test(fit, variance = "robust")
#> Provider tests: wald statistic, robust variance; null median = -0.06783; two.sided, level 0.95
#>   20 providers: 7 above, 8 below, 5 not different, 0 not tested

#>      P003   0.3252 0.24915   -0.06783     1.578 1.146e-01    0 -0.1631  0.8136
#>      P004   0.4046 0.11173   -0.06783     4.229 2.352e-05    1  0.1856  0.6236
#>      P005   0.4156 0.12481   -0.06783     3.873 1.074e-04    1  0.1710  0.6602
#>      P006  -0.3679 0.08349   -0.06783    -3.594 3.252e-04   -1 -0.5316 -0.2043
